# M5 task 9 — the analytic models on PB24

*Generated by `design/py/run_pb24_validation.py` on 200 realisations (259986 samples), stride 1. rRMS %, in `rrs` space, lower is better.*

**O25 is a refit, not the published model**, and it is refit on **each split's own training mask**. Its coefficients span the full `(theta_s, theta_v, dphi)` grid (task 8) and it is scored through the fitted surface transfer (task 7); with the nadir transfer the interface error swamps the comparison and O25 looks ~3x worse than it is.

## Every model on every split

| model | realisation (train) | realisation (held out) | bp_band (train) | bp_band (held out) | geometry (train) | geometry (held out) | non-physical % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| standard Gordon | 20.99 | 20.41 | 20.89 | 20.81 | 20.87 | 45.46 | 0.00 |
| ZTT backbone | 41116.22 | 7060.89 | 25840.01 | 64352.21 | 36910.79 | 20333.89 | 22.32 |
| O25 form, refit on PB24 | 6.38 | 6.53 | 6.48 | 6.02 | 6.41 | 22.46 | 0.00 |

The last column is the share of predicted `rrs` values that are **zero or negative**. A model producing those is not inaccurate, it is outside its domain, and an rRMS cannot say so — the same handful of samples that dominate the RMS also conceal how many there are.

## ZTT is outside its validity domain on PB24

ZTT's `mu_infinity` comes from Twardowski & Tonizzo (2017), a fit in `bb/a` and `eta_bb`. L23 spans `bb/a` up to **0.59**; PB24 reaches **9.36**, and 5.5% of its values lie beyond anything L23 probed. Out there the fitted polynomial goes **negative** (minimum -0.2658, non-positive for 0.417% of values), which flips the sign of the `(a/bb)(1 - cos(theta_v) psi / mu_inf)` term and with it the whole denominator.

So the ZTT row above is **not a statement about the backbone's accuracy**; it is a statement that the backbone has an unstated validity domain which L23 never left and PB24 leaves routinely. Its rRMS is not even a stable quantity — measured over 50/100/200/400 realisations it ranges over 7061-18972%, because a handful of sign-flipped predictions determine it. The statistics that *are* stable: a median relative error of 15.7% (against 5.9% on L23) and a non-physical share of 22.3%.

**This matters directly for task 11.** The hybrid is `rrs_ZTT * (1 + delta)` with `|delta| <= 0.5`, so a bounded *relative* correction cannot repair a backbone that has the wrong sign — on roughly a fifth of PB24 the hybrid as constructed has nothing to correct toward. See **Q17**.
